questions.question: An analog clock face is divided into 60 equal minute marks, and the numbers 1 to 12 sit 5 marks apart, so one full turn of the minute hand is 60 minutes. The minute hand starts pointing at the 2 and moves forward (clockwise) until it points at the 7, while the hour hand stays between 9 and 10 the whole time. How much time has passed?
questions.explain: Count the gaps between the numbers, not the numbers themselves: from 2 to 7 there are 5 gaps, and each gap is 5 minutes, so 5 x 5 = 25 minutes. A common trap is doing 7 - 2 = 5 and answering 5 minutes, which counts numbers instead of the 5-minute jumps.

questions.question: An analog clock face has 60 equal minute marks, and one full turn of the minute hand is 60 minutes. The minute hand starts on the mark for 15 minutes past the hour (the number 3) and stops on the mark for 50 minutes past the hour (the number 10). The hour hand stays between 8 and 9 the whole time. What is the elapsed time?
questions.explain: Both times are in the same hour, so just subtract the minute marks: 50 - 15 = 35 minutes. The trap is adding the two numbers (15 + 50 = 65); elapsed time is the distance between the marks, so you subtract.

questions.question: An analog clock face is divided into 60 equal minute marks. The minute hand starts on the 20-minute mark and moves clockwise to the 48-minute mark, all inside the same hour. How long is that duration?
questions.explain: Count on from 20 to 48 along the marks: 20 to 40 is 20 minutes, then 40 to 48 is 8 more, so 20 + 8 = 28 minutes. Adding the two mark numbers (20 + 48 = 68) is the usual slip — the hand did not travel past the top of the clock.

questions.question: An analog clock face has 60 equal minute marks around it. The minute hand starts on the mark for 38 minutes past 4 and moves forward to the mark for 52 minutes past 4. How many minutes of elapsed time is that?
questions.explain: Count on in friendly jumps: 38 to 50 is 12 minutes, then 50 to 52 is 2 more, giving 14 minutes. Many students stop at the friendly number and answer 12, forgetting the last 2 minutes.

questions.question: Ayla gets on the SkyTrain at Metrotown at 7:52 and gets off at Waterfront at 8:19. How long was her ride?
questions.explain: Break the jump at the hour: 7:52 to 8:00 is 8 minutes, then 8:00 to 8:19 is 19 minutes, so 8 + 19 = 27 minutes. Treating clock times like plain numbers (819 - 752 = 67) is wrong because an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.

questions.question: Maya practises piano from 4:05 to 4:38. Her cousin Nico practises from 4:15 to 4:44. Who practised longer, and by how many minutes?
questions.explain: Find each duration first: Maya is 38 - 5 = 33 minutes and Nico is 44 - 15 = 29 minutes, so Maya practised 33 - 29 = 4 minutes longer. Do not compare the finish times alone — Nico finishes later but started later too.

questions.question: A movie at the Victoria library starts at 11:36 and ends at 12:09 the same day. What is the elapsed time?
questions.explain: Jump to the hour and then continue: 11:36 to 12:00 is 24 minutes, plus 9 more minutes to 12:09, so 24 + 9 = 33 minutes. Subtracting the small minute number from the big one (36 - 9 = 27) ignores that the clock rolled over to a new hour.

questions.question: Jonah puts a tray of banana muffins in the oven at 3:47 and takes it out at 4:12. How long were the muffins in the oven?
questions.explain: Count 3:47 to 4:00 as 13 minutes, then 4:00 to 4:12 as 12 minutes: 13 + 12 = 25 minutes. Lining the times up like decimals and borrowing 100 (412 - 347 = 65) is the classic error, because you must borrow 60 minutes, not 100.

questions.question: Recess at a Kamloops school runs from 9:45 to 10:20. Liam says it lasted 25 minutes because 45 - 20 = 25. What is the true elapsed time?
questions.explain: Liam subtracted the minutes in the wrong order across the hour; count forward instead: 9:45 to 10:00 is 15 minutes, plus 20 minutes more, which is 35 minutes. Whenever the hour changes, jump to the o'clock first and then add the leftover minutes.

questions.question: Sofia leaves her house in Nanaimo at 3:20 and walks straight to the bus stop, which takes her 12 minutes. She then waits at the stop until her bus pulls away at 3:47. How long did Sofia wait at the bus stop?
questions.explain: First find when she arrives: 3:20 plus 12 minutes is 3:32, then the wait is 3:32 to 3:47, which is 15 minutes. The trap is answering 27 minutes, the whole time from leaving home, which still includes the walk.

questions.question: Ravi's swim lesson at the Burnaby pool runs from 4:10 to 4:55. The coach spends the first 18 minutes on kicking drills and the rest of the lesson on free swim. How long is the free swim?
questions.explain: Two steps: the whole lesson is 55 - 10 = 45 minutes, then take away the drills, 45 - 18 = 27 minutes. Subtracting 18 from the finish-time minutes (55 - 18 = 37) skips the first step of finding the total duration.

questions.question: Noah hikes the Grouse Mountain trail from 1:38 to 2:15. He writes 215 - 138 = 77, so he says the hike took 77 minutes. What is the correct elapsed time?
questions.explain: Clock times are not plain numbers, so break the jump at the hour: 1:38 to 2:00 is 22 minutes, plus 15 minutes, giving 37 minutes. Noah borrowed 100 instead of 60, which always makes the duration look far too long.
